q: 1. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following:
options: the bottom and top ends of slump mould are parallel to each other
the axis of the mould is perpendicular to the end faces
the internal surface of the mould is kept clean and free from set cement
the mould is in the form of a frustum of hexagonal pyramid
explain: The slump mould is in the shape of a frustum of a cone (circular cross-section), not a hexagonal pyramid, making this statement incorrect.

q: 2. Slump test of concrete is a measure of its
explain: The slump test measures the consistency (workability/wetness) of fresh concrete, not any hardened property like strength.

q: 3. The amount of slump depends on
explain: Slump is a direct measure of the workability of fresh concrete; a higher slump indicates higher workability.

q: 4. The strength of concrete made with angular aggregate and rounded aggregate is practically same at the water cement ratio of
explain: As per the data referenced in this text, at a water-cement ratio of about 0.48, the strength difference between angular and rounded aggregate concrete becomes negligible.

q: 5. Slump test is the most widely used field test primarily because
options: it indicates the behaviour of fresh concrete under action of gravitational forces
of the simplicity of apparatus and test procedure
it measures consistency or wetness of mix
it ensures uniformity among different batches of similar concrete
explain: The slump test is popular in the field mainly due to the simplicity of its apparatus (a simple cone mould and tamping rod) and the ease and speed of the test procedure.

q: 6. The workability of concrete by slump test is expressed as
explain: Slump is simply a linear measurement, expressed in millimetres (mm), representing the subsidence of the concrete cone.

q: 7. The slump for beam slab is
explain: For beams and slabs, a medium workability with a slump in the range of 50-100 mm is generally recommended for proper placement and compaction.

q: 8. Strength of concrete increases with
explain: Finer cement particles have greater surface area and hydrate faster and more completely, contributing to increased strength of concrete.

q: 9. The workability may be defined as the amount of applied work required to compact the concrete to its maximum density. The principle is used in
explain: The compaction factor test is based on the principle of determining the degree of compaction achieved by a standard amount of work done in dropping concrete through a standard height, directly relating to the definition given.

q: 10. The concrete mix is said to be workable if it has
explain: Workability of a concrete mix involves multiple properties together — compactability, mobility/movability and stability against segregation — hence all of these are part of it.

q: 11. When water cement ratio is increased; workability
explain: Increasing the water cement ratio makes the mix more fluid and easier to work with, thus increasing workability (though it reduces strength).

q: 12. A concrete is said to be workable if
options: it can be easily mixed, placed and compacted
it has a tendency to segregate and bleed
explain: Workability is defined as the ease with which concrete can be mixed, transported, placed, and compacted without segregation or bleeding.

q: 13. Workability of concrete in which low water cement ratio is determined by
explain: The compaction factor test is more suitable and sensitive for measuring workability of stiff/low workability (low w/c ratio) mixes where the slump test is not effective.

q: 14. Wp and Wf are the weights of a cylinder containing partially compacted and fully compacted concrete. If the compaction factor is 0.95, the workability of concrete is
explain: A compaction factor close to 1 (such as 0.95) indicates that the partially compacted weight is very close to the fully compacted weight, meaning the concrete compacts easily and has high workability.

q: 15. For high degree of workability, the compaction factor is
explain: A high degree of workability corresponds to a compaction factor close to 1, and as per the classification used here, values above 0.92 (option 0.95) represent high workability.

q: 16. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: segregation is necessary for a workable concrete
consistency does not affect the workability of concrete
if the slump increases, workability decreases
if the concrete mix is dry, the slump is maximum
explain: None of the first four statements is technically correct: segregation is undesirable, consistency does affect workability, higher slump means higher (not lower) workability, and a dry mix gives minimum (not maximum) slump. Hence 'none of the above' is correct.

q: 17. Workability of concrete mix having very low water cement ratio should be obtained by
explain: For very dry/low water-cement ratio mixes where slump is unreliable, the compaction factor test is the more appropriate method to assess workability.

q: 18. The shrinkage of concrete
options: is proportional to water content is the mix
explain: Shrinkage in concrete is influenced together by the water content, cement content, and it accumulates further as the concrete ages, so all these factors are relevant.

q: 19. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: the quality of water governs the strength of concrete
the quality of water required for concreting, depends upon the grading of aggregate and method of compaction
10% excess of water reduces the strength of concrete by 15%
30% excess of water reduces the strength of concrete by 50%
explain: All these statements about the effect of water quality and excess water quantity on concrete strength are established facts in concrete technology, hence all are correct.

q: 20. If P, Y and Z are the weights of cement, fine aggregates and coarse aggregates respectively and W/C is the water to be added to first batch, is obtained by the equation
explain: This is the standard empirical formula (0.3p + 0.1y + 0.012z = W/C x p) used to estimate the water to be added to the first trial batch based on the absorption characteristics of the mix ingredients.

q: 21. Water cement ratio by weight is
options: Higher as compared to that by volume
Lower is compared to that by volume
explain:
Since cement is heavier than an equal volume of water, expressing the water-cement ratio by weight generally yields a lower numerical value compared to expressing it by volume.
Because cement is \(1.44\text{ times}\) denser than water, dividing the same quantities by weight yields a smaller numerical ratio

q: 22. If 50 kg of fine aggregates and 100kg of coarse aggregates re mixed in a concrete whose water cement ratio is 0.6, the weight of water required for harsh mix, is
explain: Using the standard empirical relation for harsh mixes and given the fine and coarse aggregate quantities along with the specified w/c ratio of 0.6, the calculated water requirement works out to 12 kg.

q: 23. Shrinkage in concrete can be reduced by
options: Using tight and non-absorbent from work
explain: Shrinkage can be minimized through combined measures: reducing water-cement ratio, selecting suitable low-shrinkage aggregates, and using tight, non-absorbent formwork to retain moisture.

q: 24. If water cement ratio is 0.7 by weight, then the quantity of water required in concrete while using one full bag will be
explain: With a water-cement ratio of 0.7 and one bag of cement weighing 50kg, the water required is 0.7 × 50 = 35kg.

q: 25. The shrinkage of concrete is due to a change in
explain: Shrinkage fundamentally refers to a reduction in the overall volume of the concrete mass as it loses moisture over time.

q: 26. In order to have segregation in concrete, its dropping height should be less than
explain: To avoid segregation during placement, the free-fall (dropping) height of concrete should be kept below approximately 100cm.

q: 27. For a constant water cement ratio, decrease in aggregate cement ratio causes
explain: Reducing the aggregate-cement ratio (i.e., using proportionally more cement paste relative to aggregate) at a fixed water-cement ratio increases the paste content available to lubricate the mix, thereby increasing workability.

q: 28. Minimum water cement ratio required for fully hydration of cement is
explain: A water-cement ratio of about 0.38 is theoretically required for complete hydration of cement, ensuring all cement particles react fully with water.

q: 29. Minimum water cement ratio required for full hydration of cement is
explain: Theoretically, complete hydration of cement requires a water-cement ratio of about 0.23-0.25, but the practically required minimum accounting for gel-water space is about 0.36, as given in this text.

q: 30. Low water concrete result in
explain: Insufficient water in a concrete mix produces a stiff, dry mixture that becomes very difficult to work with, resulting in non-workability.

q: 31. The test conducted by Vicat's apparatus is for
explain: The Vicat apparatus is primarily used to determine the standard consistency of cement paste (as well as setting times), matching option 'consistency' here.

q: 32. The modulus of elasticity of concrete improves with
explain: As concrete matures/ages, continued hydration increases its density and strength, which in turn improves (increases) its modulus of elasticity.

q: 33. For a given aggregate content, increasing the water cement ratio in concrete
explain: Note: while a higher water-cement ratio typically increases drying shrinkage in practice, per the book's listed answer, for a given (fixed) aggregate content increasing the water-cement ratio is stated to decrease shrinkage.

q: 34. The percentage of water for making a cement paste of normal consistency varies from
explain: Typically, the water required to achieve standard/normal consistency of cement paste ranges from about 25% to 35% by weight of cement.

q: 35. For given water content, workability decreases if the concrete aggregates contain an excess of
explain: Excess of thin, flat, elongated, or flaky particles all increase surface area and interlocking, reducing workability of concrete for a given water content, so all of these are correct.

q: 36. Water in excess of that required for chemical reaction in concrete results in
explain: Excess water beyond what's chemically required for hydration tends to rise to the surface of freshly placed concrete, a phenomenon known as bleeding.

q: 37. The basic water demand depend on
explain: The basic water demand of a concrete mix is influenced together by the quality (nature, absorption) of the materials used and the target water-cement ratio.

q: 38. For given workability the grading requiring the least amount of water is one that gives
options: greatest surface area for the given cement and aggregates
least surface area for the given cement and aggregates
lest weight for the given cement and aggregates
greatest weight for the given cement and aggregates
explain: A grading that produces the least surface area of aggregate particles (for a given volume) requires the least amount of water to wet and coat the surfaces, achieving the desired workability with minimum water.

q: 39. For constant w/c ratio if the aggregate/cement ratio is reduced, the workability of concrete
explain: Reducing the aggregate-cement ratio (i.e., using relatively more cement paste) while keeping water-cement ratio constant provides more paste to lubricate the aggregates, increasing workability.

q: 40. Slump test is done for
explain: The slump test is a standard method specifically used to assess the consistency and workability of fresh concrete.

q: 41. Vacat's apparatus is used to test the following property of concrete
explain: The Vicat apparatus is used to determine the standard consistency of cement paste, which is a fundamental property tested before other cement tests are conducted.

q: 42. The minimum water-cement ratio to obtain workable concrete is
explain: A minimum water-cement ratio of about 0.40 is generally needed to produce a concrete mix with sufficient workability for proper placement and compaction.

q: 43. The slump test of concrete is used to measure its
explain: The slump test is primarily used to assess the consistency of fresh concrete, which is an indicator of its water content and workability.

q: 44. If slump of concrete mix 70 mm, its workability is considered to be
explain: A slump value of 70 mm typically falls within the medium workability range as per standard slump classification.

q: 45. A compaction factor of 0.88 indicates that the workability of concrete mix is
explain: A compaction factor of 0.88 corresponds to the medium workability range as per the IS classification table.

q: 46. More water should not be added in the concrete mix so as to increase
explain: Adding extra water beyond the design mix raises the water-cement ratio, which in turn reduces strength and durability — so all of these are adversely affected.

q: 47. Workability of concrete may be improved by adding
explain: All these admixtures/materials - fly ash, hydrated lime, calcium chloride, and bentonite - are known to improve the workability of concrete mixes when added in appropriate quantities.

q: 48. Workability of concrete may be improved by adding
explain: Air-entraining agents, foaming agents, oily agents, and aluminium compounds are all known types of admixtures that can improve the workability of concrete when properly used.

q: 49. Workability of concrete is directly proportional to
explain: Better grading of the aggregate (proper distribution of particle sizes) results in reduced voids and less water demand, which directly improves and is proportional to workability.

q: 50. Workability of concrete is inversely proportional to
explain: As the time of transit increases, some water evaporates and initial hydration begins, causing the mix to stiffen - hence workability decreases (inversely proportional) with increasing transit time.
